In 2023, imported SAF met nearly half the 26 million gallons per year of domestic SAF consumption. (For comparison, air carriers consumed almost 20 billion gallons of jet fuel in 2023 [DOT BTS 2025]). In 2021, the United States announced a target of 3 billion gallons per year of domestically produced SAF by 2030 (EASA 2025). Although six facilities in the United States were producing SAF using the only biomass-based production process as of 2024, additional facilities producing an alternative to petroleum-based diesel, known as renewable diesel, could be converted to produce SAF. Further, other facilities are planned or under construction, including a facility in Washington state that produces 50 million gallons per year of SAF (SkyNRG n.d.). SAF can also be produced without biomass using electricity, hydrogen, and carbon dioxide (ICAO n.d.-a.). Known as e-SAF, this fuel is produced using an ASTM-approved process and can be used as a drop-in fuel in blends up to 50% (ICAO n.d.-a.), and work is underway toward making e-SAF commercially available in regions such as the E.U. (SkyPower 2025), which have limited biomass capacity relative to the United States. This aviation fuel is subject to similar risks and regulatory measures as biomass-based SAF, although there is no biomass feedstock limitation. Costs for e-SAF are estimated at 10 times greater than conventional fuel (Primrose 2025), but an NLR expert estimates that e-fuels and e-SAF will become more economically feasible in 20 years. The E.U. requires suppliers to include 1.2% of aviation fuel as e-SAF starting in 2030, gradually increasing to 35% in 2050. 84 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. In the future, SAF may be developed that is compatible only with limited aircraft. If realized, “non-drop-in” SAF presents risks of requiring a segregated fuel supply for different aircraft. 85 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
